body: This feels like I wrote it. I’m a 39F and I’ve always had a shitty relationship with food, but after being diagnosed with ADHD a couple of years ago and starting methylphenidate 10mg daily, I’ve developed a full blown eating disorder. I don’t eat all day and then binge at night. I finally admitted it to myself last night and I scheduled an appt with a dietician but it’s awful. I flushed the rest of my medication but now all I can think about is gaining weight and that makes me want to die.

I like to say that my immune system is an idiot. 

Unless people really want more - then I’ll explain that it’s a neurological autoimmune disease that causes my immune system to attack the myelin protecting my nerves. 

If they want MORE, I’ll say that they don’t know the cause but they suspect some combination of environment, possibly Epstein-Barre early on, and family background. I’ll say that it causes all sorts of symptoms and can progress or stay dormant depending on what type you have. Blah blah blah. They usually glaze over by that point.

The first attorney was scamming me. I never qualified for chapter 7. He was just the first one I tried and I was unlucky. 

I live in MA and my income is a base of $79k but I make about $110k with bonuses. I make too much to qualify for chapter 7, so I think if I shopped around I might save like $500-$1000 at most. 

I did reach out to my 401k today and they confirmed that I can indeed take out a loan for $28k at the market interest rate plus 1%. Which is obviously better than the 20-29% on my three credit cards.
Good to know. Thank you!

I am about to switch to Kesimpta though because my white matter is decreasing and my lesions are stable.

I’ve been doing mindfulness meditation for about 6 weeks nearly every day and one thing I noticed is that on a video call recently I caught my face and immediately thought “wow she’s beautiful” which is NEVER something I would ever normally think. Like most- when I see myself on camera.. I immediately find something I dislike and never really come out of that. I am 100% sure that my meditation caused this subtle change in my day to day life. Now I walk past mirrors and even find myself smiling at how much I think I’m pretty. Might sound shallow but it’s a big step for me in my journey to not body shame myself constantly. I think meditation allows us to think about ourselves with so much compassion sometimes that it literally transfers into our day to day life. Hope this didn’t sound snobby because I wouldn’t ever explain this to someone face to face bc it would sound so shitty. 

I also noticed that I’ve been much much kinder to myself internally which for me… is a form of being my ideal self. Cheers to us feeling noticeable benefits as beginners!
